_comment: This app's own 12-row verdict against advisor-model.json's functionality table - rendered by buildTrail.js as Act 2, 'Why this stack'. Written by hand rather than derived by running js/advisor.js on this app's own intake answers, so the build trail can explain each row in this app's own words (a generic auto-derivation would only restate the functionality table, not argue for a rung).

rows.why: The whole page - map, charts, build trail, advisor - is one static index.html.
A polished look for a business-readable page, no build step - the exact route use-cases.md's audience table recommends for a read-only business audience.
Zoom/pan, hover tooltips, click-through detail cards, and cross-filtering the map with both companion charts - all without a page reload.
Nothing outside this page needs to call this app for data.
The page fetches its own static JSON/TopoJSON files, not a live API - that is functionality 1 (presentation) serving pre-built data, not functionality 5.
No per-request server compute - every aggregate (region totals, the top-15 ranking) is computed once in the browser from the static data, in js/data.js.
Nothing is saved. The terminal dataset is a build-time research artifact (data/terminals.json), not a database.
No create/edit/delete of any record - the page is read-only.
No accounts. Every visitor sees the same public data.
No per-user visibility to enforce - see 9.
The current filter/selection lives in js/app.js's in-memory state for the length of one page view; nothing is remembered across visits, so there is no session to manage.
Every computation here finishes well under a second - see references/background-jobs.md for when this would flip.

escalationTriggers: Reviewers needing accounts to comment on or curate terminals → escalation D-1 (Streamlit/Dash to Django) - except this app has no server-side compute to begin with, so it would first need to grow into rung 2 or 3.

Live PSA throughput figures replacing this dataset's static, dated snapshot → rung 3, a small API (functionality 4) serving fresher data to the same D3 front end - see this README's 'Out of scope' section.
The build trail or advisor wanting to save a visitor's own scenario → functionality 7 (persistence), which nothing here currently needs.
